chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked about the man upon whom zakat becomes due during the year at three times: does he delay it until he pays it at one time? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it becomes due, he should extract it.'
And regarding zakat on wheat, barley, dates, and raisins: when does it become obligatory upon its owner? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he harvests it, and when he evaluates it.'
ai.seo_question: When does zakat become obligatory on crops like wheat and dates according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that zakat on agricultural produce becomes obligatory at the precise moment of harvest and valuation (kharas), rejecting the practice of delaying payment to consolidate multiple annual obligations into a single disbursement. This ruling underscores the principle of immediacy in fulfilling financial worship, ensuring that the poor receive their due without unnecessary postponement by the payer.
